steps.content: [Inside the Lighthouse] [Dizzy Heartbeats]

steps.speaker: Voice in Mind
steps.content: ...You survived again. Burden... Luck... A coward's pulse... You're all alone now...

steps.speaker: Voice in Mind
steps.content: He stopped you... defiled a soldier's destiny, dragging you back into the mire... You belong to death, and so does he... kill him... kill him...
steps.female_content: She stopped you... defiled a soldier's destiny, dragging you back into the mire... You belong to death, and so does she... kill her... kill her...

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: ...

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Shut up, damn blade...

Her eyelids are leaden, her vision a dark, rising tide. Only blurry shapes of light remain, swaying in the gloom. The lighthouse air is humid and cold, the walls themselves sweating the salty scent of the Black Tide. Through the haze, a shadow moves with busy intent.
A confused thought surfaces: wasn't she alone? Wasn't she the last one left?
Stay with me. Don't pass out on me again. I need to stop the bleeding.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: You...
She attempts to rise, but her body is a weak, sore ache. The fragile figure before her wavers and splits, a maddening blur that grates on her frayed nerves.
Don't move. One of those things got you good. Black Tide got in the wound. The Mania contamination's spreading.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Also, the Bureau will pay for the subsequent restoration costs and admission fees.
Maybe not, but it still hurts like hell. The wound's on your back. Turn around and take your jacket off. I've got a little clean water to rinse it...

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Stop nagging!
With a sudden surge of strength, she fists a hand in your collar and yanks you close. Your labored breath washes hot against each other, and finally, recognition crashes into her eyes.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I know!
She cuts you off, her grip locking onto your wrist with brutal force. You gasp at the sudden, sharp pain.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: The bandages... take them off.
What?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: From last night. The wound...

steps.speaker: Voice in Mind
steps.content: Pathetic... pitiful... Look at yourself... A monster. This is what you've become...

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Hurry!
Her knife flashes, a sharp sting as she slices your palm open, tearing through the old wound. Fresh blood soaks the crude bandage in an instant.

There's no time to react. Her hot, frantic breath is already on your skin. You feel the pull as your blood is drawn out, a strange, tingling suction. The sound of swallowing is deafening this close to your ear; the sweet, metallic scent thickens the air... Your thoughts dissolve into static.
And with it, fragmented, burning memories rip into your mind—not like a gentle flow, but like a net being violently torn open.
[Flashback] [White Screen Consciousness World]

steps.speaker: Lia
steps.content: Heeeey, DisCity! Can you hear me? I'm going to save so many people! I'm going to be a real hero!

steps.speaker: Rode
steps.content: I get to come home this year! Just... just everyone stay safe! Let everything go smoothly!

steps.speaker: Miles
steps.content: You hear that, all you jerks who looked down on me? When I get back, you'll be bowing your heads!

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: I... I want my little girl to be proud of me! She's going to have a father she can look up to!

steps.speaker: Fynn
steps.content: You hear that? We're all coming back in glory!

steps.speaker: Fynn
steps.content: Our rallying cry is...

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: Since when did we get a rallying cry?

steps.speaker: Fynn
steps.content: Oh, come on! We'll make one up! Don't be so rigid. Hmm... got it! Repeat after me!

steps.speaker: Fynn
steps.content: For hope, for dawn, for every soul—

steps.speaker: Lia
steps.content: Aren't those just lyrics from a song?

steps.speaker: Rode
steps.content: Impressive, I can't believe you recognize such an old song.

steps.speaker: Fynn
steps.content: Hey! Who are you calling old? Watch it, or I'll make you run laps!

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: Okay, okay, easy now. You always overreact. I've heard the song too... Why don't we just sing it together?

steps.speaker: Fynn
steps.content: Wait, we're missing someone. Ceto! Come over here! We'll teach you how to sing it—
There once were all the prayers For our loved ones, keeping the light Here comes every victory For hope, for dawn, for every soul

steps.speaker: Rode
steps.content: Ceto, stay back! Go... find the Captain. Now!

steps.speaker: Lia
steps.content: I can't... I don't know what to do! Ceto, help me, I don't want to—

steps.speaker: Fynn
steps.content: Lead the others and keep them alive. You are our hope now...
Ceto jerks upright, her gaze darting aimlessly around the room before snapping into focus the moment it meets yours.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Why are you here?
Who did you think I was?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Don't ask questions you shouldn't. And stop making assumptions.
A former lighthouse keeper?

Her eyes fall on the wound in your palm, as she feels the strange warmth still tingling on her own lips. She offers no retort to your question, an unusual silence broken only by her awkward glance toward the table.
There, resting between you, is the dagger she always carries.

Relax, I didn't lay a hand on you. You made it clear you didn't want your wound treated, so I backed off. Didn't touch your knife, either. The shackles... they just react on their own when you... tried to harm me.
You, a person from DisCity, take it all in stride. Nothing about what happened seems to shock you; in fact, your gaze upon the blade holds a trace of familiarity.
This might sound strange, but I have a special connection with the <color=#fb9259>Rancors</color>. Like your knife. Sometimes... I can see things. Fragments of their history.
Unfortunately, without any proper gear out here, it's just vague impressions.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Cut the mystical crap. If you've got something to say, say it. I'm not in the mood for games.

options: I saw pieces of your past.
I can hear the Rancor's voice.

steps.content: The keepers were part of DisCity's Rancor division. But according to what I knew before coming here, they were completely wiped out in N.F. 84.
But your knife tells a different story. That a few survived. Held the lighthouses, waiting for a rescue from DisCity that never came. Taking heavy losses all the while.
You weren't just stranded and starving. You were fighting the Rancors' influence itself. From the moment you pick those weapons up, they never stop whispering in your mind...
They want blood. Slaughter... They want to hollow you out, turn you into a bloodthirsty puppet—

steps.speaker: Rancors
steps.content: Give me blood! Kill him! All of this is meaningless!
steps.female_content: Give me blood! Kill her! All of this is meaningless!

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Enough!
The screams that have haunted her for a decade echo in her mind. In a flash, Ceto snatches the knife back from you.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I don't care what you think you know. This is none of your business.
She rises and strides toward the door. You stop her just as her hand reaches for the handle.
So you can go throw yourself at the monsters again? Like yesterday? Is this a new death wish, or... have you just been bad at succeeding all this time?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I don't know what you're talking about. I'm going to guard the lighthouse. It's my duty.
You kept me out of the lantern room today. You set the beacon to signal abandonment, didn't you? I don't know why you're giving up, but stopping you from self-destructing is my duty.
Straightening your coat, you turn to face her, your expression solemn, and extend your hand.
I am the Chief of DisCity MBCC, an advisor to the Rancor squad, tasked with retrieving the remaining Rancors from the WhiteSands border.
I'm here to bring the Rancors home.
For the first time, you witness a complex flood of emotions cross Ceto's face. She struggles to steady her breathing, visibly fighting the urge to bombard you with questions.
You offer her a long silence, refusing to press her.
You understand their resentment. How long had the keepers stood their post—ten years? Twenty? However time was measured here, their story was one of abandonment by DisCity.

Outside, rain patters relentlessly against the windows. Monsters growl and prowl the shoreline, waiting for the tide to recede. Inside the lighthouse, an unnatural silence hangs thick in the air. Then, suddenly...
A deafening explosion erupts from above.
[Beach Lighthouse]
The lone Sun amid the Black Tide, your only hope for rescue, Ceto's last remaining anchor—

Lighthouse OT-N07, which had never faltered since the Black Tide outbreak, is extinguished. On the night of July 13, N.F. 115, it has suffered critical damage under the attack of the Tide Crawlers and gone dark.
The solitary island is plunged into absolute blackness.
